question: In April 2022, the Commission officially declared that Russian students, researchers and academics continued to be eligible to take part in the Erasmus and Horizon programmes1. In August 2022, the European External Action Service (EEAS) announced that Russian students would receive 66 Erasmus grants.

At the same time, 204 000 Hungarian students and some 20 000 lecturers and researchers from 21 universities were excluded from the Erasmus and Horizon programmes2. It has recently come to our attention that the Commission plans to extend these programmes to countries in Africa and the Middle East as part of the Pact for the Mediterranean.
Commissioner Šuica referred specifically to the intention to ‘scale up talent partnerships with Morocco, with Tunisia and with Egypt’3. In view of the above: 1.
Can the Commission explain why students, teachers and researchers from Russia are eligible to take part in the Erasmus and Horizon programmes, but those from 21 Hungarian universities are not?
Does the Commission consider the standards of democratic governance and the rule of law in Morocco to be more closely aligned with the values of the European Union than those observed in Hungary?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.3.2026) Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/2506 of 15 December 20221 sets out the measures for the protection of the EU budget against breaches of the principles of the rule of law in Hungary.

The measures are proportionate and temporary, pending Hungary’s remedy of identified rule of law deficiencies, in particular the risks of conflicts of interests in the boards of so-called ‘public interest trusts’2.

The cooperation with legal person, entity or body established in Russia was restricted following Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and it is prohibited to provide direct or indirect support, including financing and financial assistance or any other benefit, to the categories of entities listed in Article 5(l) paragraph 1 (a) and (b) of Council Regulation (EU) No 833/20143.

Researcher mobility for persons established in Russia under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions of Horizon Europe4 has been suspended, as has academic staff mobility under Erasmus+. The only remaining form of participation of students from Russia falls under the exception set out in Article 5(l) paragraph 2(e) concerning mobility exchanges for individuals and people-to-people contacts.

This very limited participation is kept under continuous review; it is the subject of a dedicated assessment to grant the exception and may be further restricted should the sanctions framework evolve.

Partners from Southern Mediterranean countries continue to benefit from the already existing opportunities under the relevant actions of the Erasmus+ programme, funded through additional budget from the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument -Global Europe5. The Commission is committed to ensure that no one receives EU funding if involved in any activities incompatible with EU values.
